text:
alex: Heads-up — ap-south1 machines showing repeated nvme IOPS spikes over the last 30m. Correlates with long-context chat workloads where KV cache unexpectedly grows. GPU attach queue jumped and some pods got stuck.

maria: noticed. metrics: nvme_iops 3x baseline during spike, write-amplification up ~2.2x. Attach latency +120s on average.

jun: any error logs from janitor/evictor? could be cleaner kicking off when cache hot.

alex: paste from node logs:```
[2026-03-23T10:12:03Z] kvcache: resize triggered (delta=1.2GB)
[2026-03-23T10:12:03Z] janitor: schedule scrub window start
[2026-03-23T10:12:04Z] nvme: iosubmit backlog spike -> iops=185k
[2026-03-23T10:12:05Z] gpu-attach: backoff start (reason=ephemeral-io)
```

priya: opsbot alerted earlier: "IOPS_SURGE ap-south1 10:11" — ops runbook suggests limiting janitor concurrency or toggling cache growth policy.

opsbot: @channel IOPS_SURGE detected for cluster ap-south1-ephemeral. Recommended actions: 1) throttle kvcache growth, 2) reduce janitor concurrency to 1, 3) pause non-critical backfills.

sam: quick mitigation we can do: flip kvcache soft-limit from 4GB -> 1.5GB for the affected cohort and scale janitor from 4->1. I'll prepare rollout.

maria: agree. small experiment: throttle growth + drop janitor concurrency. If attach backlog clears in 5-10m we keep.

jun: long-term: we should detect cache growth patterns by model type (long-context vs short). Maybe auto-evict prefixes older than 24h, not just LRU. Also consider batching/combining cache writes to reduce write amplification.

alex: cost angle — if this repeats we'll either need more Dedicated capacity in ap-south1 (reserve to avoid attach churn) or invest in better on-node cache eviction heuristics. Dedicated increases monthly commit by ~$8k/month for the region. Throttling risks higher latency. Thoughts?

priya: pinging product infra folks, but short-term we should avoid buying capacity until we confirm pattern persists. Ops: do mitigation, collect 6h trace, then decide.

sam: rolling kvcache soft-limit now on 6 nodes in the hot cohort. Command: `for node in $(nodes -l hot); do ssh $node sudo /usr/local/bin/set-kvcache --soft-limit=1.5G; done`

alex: thanks. also pausing non-critical janitor runs: `kubectl label node <node> janitor-paused=true` for the cohort.

maria: 3m after change: nvme_iops back down to ~1.1x baseline, attach backlog decreased from 42 -> 6. Looks promising.

jun: capture traces and share repro scripts. I'll open a short-lived canary job to try to recreate under controlled conditions.

priya: filing follow-up action items: [1] 6h perf trace (sam), [2] eviction heuristic proposal (jun), [3] cost vs capacity analysis for ap-south1 (product/finance), [4] runbook update to include kvcache throttles (ops).

alex: nice work. moving to monitoring watch for 12h and then run the postmortem if this recurs. :thumbsup:

maria: FYI — adding alert tweak: only page SRE if attach_backlog > 60 for 10m (reduce noisy pages).
